name: Capstone-Disney-World-Date-and-Attendance-Predictor
what_it_holds: 12 CSVs of daily average ride wait times (resampled from 5-10 minute readings) for rides across all four Walt Disney World parks (Magic Kingdom x3, Epcot x2, Hollywood Studios x3, Animal Kingdom x4), covering Jan 2015-Dec 2021 (analysis window 2015-2019). Original data pulled from touringplans.com's public crowd-calendar dataset.
why_useful: Ride wait times are a well-established public proxy for theme-park crowd levels/attendance (touringplans.com dataset used in academic tourism-demand papers); gives a long, daily, US leisure-travel demand series independent of Airbnb, useful as a domestic discretionary-travel cross-check alongside TSA and NPS series.
size_hint: 12 CSV files, multi-year daily series per ride
license: not stated; underlying source touringplans.com is a known open dataset
themes: Destination demand proxies: US National Park Service visitation stats API, state park attendance, museum/theme-park attendance, ski resort data, beach visitation
why_all: Ride wait times are a well-established public proxy for theme-park crowd levels/attendance (touringplans.com dataset used in academic tourism-demand papers); gives a long, daily, US leisure-travel demand series independent of Airbnb, useful as a domestic discretionary-travel cross-check alongside TSA and NPS series.

name: ticketpy (Ticketmaster Discovery API Python wrapper)
what_it_holds: Python SDK/wrapper (29 stars) for the Ticketmaster Discovery API, which exposes event listings (concerts, sports, festivals) with venue, date, and location metadata across the US and internationally where Ticketmaster operates.
why_useful: A ready client for pulling event density by city/date as an events/shocks proxy (gap #11: FIFA World Cup 2026, concerts, conferences) that could feed a city-level event calendar to explain short-term nights/ADR spikes; requires a free Ticketmaster Discovery API key, no scraping of a login-walled site.
last_activity: unspecified, low star count suggests light maintenance
time_coverage: forward-looking event calendar, not historical panel
themes: Restaurant and leisure proxies: OpenTable state of the industry CSV, Yelp dataset, Google Maps reviews scrapers, event ticket data
why_all: A ready client for pulling event density by city/date as an events/shocks proxy (gap #11: FIFA World Cup 2026, concerts, conferences) that could feed a city-level event calendar to explain short-term nights/ADR spikes; requires a free Ticketmaster Discovery API key, no scraping of a login-walled site.
Same events-calendar use case as ticketpy above (gap #11) if the official API's coverage or rate limits are insufficient; runs on Apify's platform rather than being a self-contained repo.

name: world-cup-2026-calendar
what_it_holds: Single committed FIFA_World_Cup_2026.ics file (~40KB), all 104 matches numbered WC2026 #1-#104, group letters A-L, kickoff times in US Eastern, venue and host city for every match (Estadio Azteca, MetLife Stadium, BMO Field, AT&T Stadium, etc.) across US/Canada/Mexico, Jun 11-Jul 19 2026. MIT license, 6 stars, updated 23 Jul 2026.
why_useful: Same schedule/host-city gap as above but as a clean, single-file calendar (easy to parse to a date x host-metro table) rather than a relational dataset -- a cheap cross-check/alternate source for the World Cup demand-shock calendar feeding 3Q26 forecasts.
themes: Event calendars: FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule and host-city data, Olympics, concerts (Setlist.fm, Songkick, Ticketmaster API), conferences, PredictHQ samples, holiday calendars by country
why_all: Same schedule/host-city gap as above but as a clean, single-file calendar (easy to parse to a date x host-metro table) rather than a relational dataset -- a cheap cross-check/alternate source for the World Cup demand-shock calendar feeding 3Q26 forecasts.

name: phq-data-science-docs
what_it_holds: PredictHQ's data-science documentation repo (MIT, 17 stars) with articles and linked downloadable Jupyter notebooks demonstrating how to build demand-forecasting features from event data (attendance impact, event density nowcasting). No committed CSV/parquet in the repo itself -- notebooks are linked externally.
why_useful: Could contain worked examples of turning event calendars into demand features (analogous to what we'd want for World Cup / conferences / holidays feeding nights forecasts) even without a full data export.
themes: Event calendars: FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule and host-city data, Olympics, concerts (Setlist.fm, Songkick, Ticketmaster API), conferences, PredictHQ samples, holiday calendars by country
Corporate travel and business-travel data (GBTA, Concur/SAP, Navan public indices, conference calendars), MICE datasets
wildcard: an Airbnb superhost / small property manager who uses open-s
why_all: Could contain worked examples of turning event calendars into demand features (analogous to what we'd want for World Cup / conferences / holidays feeding nights forecasts) even without a full data export.

Shows worked examples of how an events-impact feed could be joined to demand series (methodological reference for building our own event-shock feature even if we don't buy PredictHQ), but supplies no standalone data.

Worked methodology for turning an event calendar (including MICE/conference events) into a demand-nowcasting feature -- relevant to gap #17 (nowcasting methods) if the team ever builds an event-density regressor for business-travel markets.
Companion methods doc to sdk-py; useful as a template for building an events-based demand feature set for ABNB nights/ADR nowcasting without re-deriving the feature engineering from scratch.

name: streamlit-accommodation-demo
what_it_holds: Streamlit demo app pulling PredictHQ event data specifically for accommodation-demand forecasting (per the repo purpose: 'Streamlit Accommodation Demo App'). No committed dataset (needs API key), but the method -- event calendar -> accommodation demand -- is exactly the ABNB use case.
why_useful: A worked reference implementation for turning an event calendar (concerts/conferences/sports) into an accommodation-demand signal, i.e. a template method for the World Cup/holiday/conference demand-shock work, even though it requires a paid/free-tier PredictHQ key to run.
themes: Event calendars: FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule and host-city data, Olympics, concerts (Setlist.fm, Songkick, Ticketmaster API), conferences, PredictHQ samples, holiday calendars by country
wildcard: an Airbnb superhost / small property manager who uses open-s
why_all: A worked reference implementation for turning an event calendar (concerts/conferences/sports) into an accommodation-demand signal, i.e. a template method for the World Cup/holiday/conference demand-shock work, even though it requires a paid/free-tier PredictHQ key to run.

Confirms PredictHQ explicitly markets an accommodation-demand use case (i.e. this is exactly what STR pricing tools ingest) and gives a runnable reference implementation for pulling an events-based demand index by market — useful scaffolding rather than a dataset.
